name: Poll / Opinion Vote
summary: No correct answer. Learners select from options or type a short response; results are visualized as a chart or word cloud.

aiGenerability.notes: AI generates opinion prompts easily. No grading or evaluation needed—pure mechanic. Can generate multiple-choice opinion options or open-ended prompts. Trivial to implement; high engagement.

prompt.description: The opinion/reflection question. e.g., 'Which invention changed the world most?' or 'What surprised you today?' or 'Which would you choose: more time or more money?'

options.description: For closed variant: array of 3-5 opinion options. For open variant (word cloud), omit this.

ux.mobileNotes: Fast tap interaction. Show poll options as large, tappable buttons. Results should appear instantly or with a satisfying animation (bars grow, words scatter into cloud). Can show live results (updating as other learners vote) or reveal all at once after learner votes. Mobile-friendly display of charts (no small legends, large fonts).

ageAdaptations.8-10: Fun, engaging opinion questions with 3-4 clear options. Topics are lighthearted or personally relevant ('What's your favorite animal?', 'Would you rather...?', 'Which season is best?'). Results shown as a simple bar chart with large numbers or emoji. No open-ended text variant.
ageAdaptations.11-13: More reflective opinion questions that prompt thinking about the lesson ('Which character made the best choice?', 'What do you think will happen next?', 'Which source is most trustworthy?'). 4-5 options or open-ended word cloud variant. Results shown as bar chart or pie chart with percentages.
ageAdaptations.14-16: Sophisticated opinion and meta-cognitive questions ('Which of these arguments is most compelling?', 'What is your biggest takeaway?'). Often open-ended (word cloud) to allow complex responses. Results can include filtering, sorting, or thematic tagging (e.g., showing common themes in responses). Encourages class discussion about divergent opinions.
